answer: Registry weight is a cut, not a key: a head counts only if removing its vertex adds one island to the public graph, with sable locked on that vertex. Heads from one operator that fall to the same island are one voice. The first head locks 1 sable; each further head must sit beyond all prior still-paid cuts and double the lock, all burned if any two share an island. Honest head: one vertex, 1 sable. Faking n means n disjoint cuts and 2^n−1 sable; a fresh key lands islandless.
